title: Libya Pipeline Blockade Costs $31M as Bahrain Industrial Site Hit, AI Boom Forces Grid Overhaul, and UK Rewrites Nuclear Rules
subhead: Libya's National Oil Corporation warned a 20-day pipeline blockade has cost nearly $31 million as Iranian strikes hit an industrial site in Bahrain, while AI data center demand is forcing massive global power grid upgrades and Britain moves to rewrite nuclear licensing rules by 2027.

sections.heading: Libya Pipeline Blockade Costs $31M as Bahrain Industrial Site Hit by Iran
sections.body:
Libya's National Oil Corporation warned that a blockade of the Hamada-Zawiya oil pipeline lasting more than 20 days has cost the country nearly $31 million and shut in over 302,000 barrels of crude output, Anadolu Agency reports. The disruption adds supply friction in North Africa at a time when Gulf energy corridors remain under attack.

In the Persian Gulf, Bahrain said an Iranian drone and missile attack damaged an industrial facility, while Iran's IRGC claimed it targeted US positions, Times of Israel reports. Meanwhile, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said a US-Iran deal is vital to easing global financial crises and confirmed diplomatic efforts around the Strait of Hormuz continue despite deadlock, Anadolu Agency reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Sustained pipeline shut-ins in Libya and attacks on Gulf industrial infrastructure keep physical supply risks elevated even when global oil benchmarks soften on surplus forecasts.

sections.heading: AI Boom Drives 10,000 TWh Electricity Surge and Global Grid Investment
sections.body:
Rapid expansion in artificial intelligence and information technology is projected to drive global electricity demand up by more than 10,000 TWh over the next decade, forcing urgent worldwide investment in power grid upgrades, OilPrice reports citing World Energy Outlook projections. Policymakers and utilities remain divided over whether hyperscalers or ratepayers will absorb the multibillion-dollar transmission costs.

Looking at generation economics, think tank Ember reported that pairing wind power with solar and battery storage could cut the cost of round-the-clock clean electricity by 18%, calling slower wind deployment a major missed opportunity for energy security, OilPrice notes.
sections.whyItMatters: Grid congestion—not generation hardware alone—is emerging as the primary bottleneck for AI data center expansion and industrial electrification through the 2030s.

sections.heading: UK Races to Rewrite Nuclear Rules by 2027 Amid China Supply Chain Concerns
sections.body:
The British government aims to rewrite nuclear regulatory rules by 2027 to accelerate reactor approvals and diversify its decarbonized power mix alongside renewables, OilPrice reports. At the same time, UK officials face sharp domestic criticism over clean-tech supply dependencies on China, with a new report warning of national security risks across Britain's net-zero transition.

In Australia, energy analysts warned that Victoria faces a serious electricity supply gap and bill shocks when the Yallourn coal-fired power station closes in 2028, as neither Labor nor the opposition Coalition has presented adequate replacement capacity plans, The Guardian reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Streamlining nuclear permitting in the UK and looming coal-exit gaps in Australia show Western grids struggling to balance decarbonization deadlines with baseload reliability.

sections.heading: US Coal Revival Raises Consumer Costs as Thanksgiving Gas Prices Near Records
sections.body:
President Trump's federal interventions to halt scheduled US coal plant retirements are costing American taxpayers and electricity consumers more than projected, according to an OilPrice analysis of plant-subsidy expenses. Separately, although US retail gasoline prices dropped nearly 60 cents over the past month to a national average of $3.69 per gallon on Friday, GasBuddy projects Americans could still pay record Thanksgiving pump prices, OilPrice reports.

On the upstream side, Baker Hughes data cited by Anadolu Agency showed the US active oil rig count rose by 6 to 469 in the week ending November 20, while Alberta tweaked its carbon capture incentive program to allow grants during construction, CityNews Calgary reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Keeping aging coal plants online and elevated seasonal fuel costs demonstrate how domestic energy interventions are feeding directly into US household utility and transport bills.

sections.heading: China Expands Latin America Minerals Footprint; Argentina Bond Rush Accelerates
sections.body:
China is steadily expanding its economic footprint across Latin America through port infrastructure, trade financing, and critical minerals agreements, Latin Times reports, while Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia opened talks on joint critical minerals and mining cooperation to diversify supply routes, Trend News Agency notes.

In South America, Argentine energy companies are rushing to issue corporate bonds ahead of the 2027 election cycle to lock in financing after surging Vaca Muerta shale oil and gas exports delivered Argentina's strongest half-year energy trade balance in five years, OilPrice reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Beijing's port and mineral diplomacy alongside Vaca Muerta's export boom underscore Latin America's growing weight in both critical mineral supply chains and non-OPEC hydrocarbon growth.

bottomLine: Libya's $31 million pipeline blockade and Iranian strikes in Bahrain keep physical supply routes vulnerable, while AI-driven grid expansion demands, UK nuclear deregulation, and rising US coal-subsidy costs force governments to rethink reliability and financing.
sources: Anadolu Agency, Times of Israel, OilPrice, The Guardian, CityNews Calgary, Latin Times, Trend News Agency
